sentences.t: Have you ever wondered how a child learns to speak without a single grammar lesson?
Researchers say the answer is simple: children listen a lot, long before they say their first word.
By the age of one, they already recognize many common words and the rhythm of their language.
They make mistakes, such as saying "I goed" instead of "I went", but adults rarely correct them harshly.
Instead, they smile and say the right word naturally.
This is important, because fear of mistakes is one of the biggest obstacles for adult learners.
Children do not feel embarrassed, so they keep trying.
A child hears the same song or story dozens of times, and each time the language sinks in a little deeper.
First, listen every day, even if you do not understand everything.
Second, repeat out loud, just like a child would.
Third, give yourself permission to make mistakes.
They are not failures; they are proof that you are learning.
Science cannot make you a child again, but it can show you a better way to learn.
Be patient, be curious, and keep playing with the language.
